title: SOURCE_TARGETS retired: user-management ExecuteInternal uses isolated sys session

analysis: executeAlterUser obtains sysSession via e.GetSysSession() and sets sqlExecutor := sysSession.GetSQLExecutor() before readPasswordLockingInfo, isRole, UPDATE mysql.user, and related ExecuteInternal calls
BaseExecutor.GetSysSession obtains a separate domain sys session and marks it InRestrictedSQL; it does not run internal SQL on the user's session that submitted ALTER USER
the user session's pending TxnReadTS/SnapshotInfoschema therefore does not enter the internal mysql.user reads/writes
the same pattern applies to nearby CREATE USER/GRANT/REVOKE style user-management statements that use GetSysSession before ExecuteInternal
source_anchors: pkg/executor/simple.go:1759-1764 executeAlterUser obtains sysSession and sqlExecutor from it
pkg/executor/internal/exec/executor.go:568-577 GetSysSession obtains a separate sys session
payload.why_not_execute: A RED would require injecting pending TxnReadTS into the sys session itself, which is not a user-visible state-ingress schedule.
payload.next_step: negative cache for state-ingress generator; downgrade or skip candidates whose ExecuteInternal is behind GetSysSession unless there is an explicit state-copy boundary
